name: Chip Fabrication
blurb: Who actually manufactures AI silicon, on what process, and where.

items.name: GlobalFoundries
items.note: Trailing-edge and specialty nodes; the US-based volume foundry for everything that does not need leading edge

items.name: Intel Foundry
items.note: Intel's external foundry business; 18A is its leading-edge node bid for AI silicon

items.name: Samsung Foundry
items.note: The second leading-edge logic foundry; gate-all-around SF3/SF2 nodes

items.name: SMIC
items.note: China's leading foundry and the fabrication path for domestic AI accelerators under export controls

items.name: TSMC
items.note: Fabricates nearly every leading AI accelerator - NVIDIA, AMD, Apple, Google TPU - on N5/N4/N3 nodes; corporate site bot-walls verification, so the source is its SEC 20-F filing index

reading.body:
TSMC fabricates nearly every leading AI accelerator on the market, making a single company in Taiwan the dominant physical chokepoint between AI ambition and deployed compute.

The five foundries listed divide into three tiers by process capability. TSMC sits alone at the top, producing chips for NVIDIA, AMD, Apple, and Google on N5, N4, and N3 nodes. Samsung Foundry competes at leading edge with its gate-all-around SF3 and SF2 processes. Intel Foundry is attempting to re-enter that tier with its 18A node. GlobalFoundries serves a different market entirely, supplying trailing-edge and specialty nodes for applications that do not require the density of AI accelerators. SMIC occupies a distinct position as the fabrication path available to Chinese AI chip designers operating under export controls.

The concentration at TSMC matters for AI scaling because leading-edge node access is not substitutable in the short term. A data center building can be constructed in months, and power capacity can be added faster than it historically has been, but advanced semiconductor process capability takes years and tens of billions of dollars to establish. The data covers only five foundries and does not address packaging, which is a separate constraint for high-bandwidth memory integration, nor does it capture equipment suppliers or the geographic distribution of fab capacity within each company.
